title: Daily arXiv Biology and Biomedicine — 2026-11-06
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance ranking, not a popularity ranking, and arXiv’s biomedical coverage is incomplete. Many clinical and experimental biology preprints appear on bioRxiv or medRxiv.

sections.title: Headline
sections.summary: Friday’s 6 November 2026 arXiv biology/biomedicine batch yielded seven notable papers from 15 eligible announcement records (14 new submissions and one revision). The dominant pattern is biological AI being evaluated against harder benchmarks, with one drug-discovery system reporting human-run experimental follow-up. Spoken agenda: agent-assisted drug discovery, protein design, single-cell genomics, docking, colorectal-risk prediction, MRI harmonization, and intracellular reaction networks.
sections.global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance ranking, not a popularity ranking, and arXiv’s biomedical coverage is incomplete.

sections.title: PharmAgents2: Towards Autonomous End-to-End Drug Discovery
sections.abstract: PharmAgents2 combines extracted scientific decision knowledge with parallel agents for drug-discovery planning; its authors report three candidate-generation studies followed by human-executed experiments.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a 121-question benchmark and three end-to-end tasks. Follow-up included 63 purchased LpxH candidates, 34 JAK1 candidates tested in cytokine-signalling assays, and SPR evidence supporting binding of a proposed secondary target for another molecule.
sections.unique_caveat: Experiments were executed by human researchers, not autonomously. The proposed LpxH site and mechanism remain under validation; the findings do not establish therapeutic efficacy, safety, or clinical utility.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct drug-discovery relevance and author-reported biochemical, cellular, and binding-assay follow-up in three studies; relevance and contribution signals, not popularity measures.

sections.title: Static Recovery Is Not Dynamic Stability: Dynamics-Aware Benchmarking of Protein Motif Scaffolding
sections.abstract: BILBY adds a PROSITE-derived motif-scaffolding benchmark and molecular-dynamics checks to test whether static protein-motif recovery corresponds to dynamical stability.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce BILBY-PRO with 220 cases from 174 PROSITE motif-pattern entries and BILBY-MD. Of 55 statically solved pairs assessed with MD, 31 met the MD-supported criterion and 8 passed all checks.
sections.unique_caveat: The MD-support thresholds are heuristic and 200 ns design trajectories may miss slower instabilities; the evaluation is computational, not experimental functional validation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations & Datasets Track); reports a 220-case benchmark and dynamics evaluation on 55 statically solved model–problem pairs.

sections.title: MUSS: A Multi-scale and Sequence-based Model for Single-cell Gene Regulation
sections.abstract: MUSS integrates DNA-sequence representations with chromatin accessibility and paired single-cell expression data to model gene regulation across sequence and cell scales.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report results against sequence and single-cell baselines for expression prediction, enhancer–gene linking, motif-guided prioritization, and zero-shot cell clustering, including tests on unseen genes and peaks.
sections.unique_caveat: Results are computational, not causal or experimental validation. The authors note reliance on a frozen sequence encoder and paired multi-omic data, quadratic attention cost, and single-run estimates for some expression outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct genomics fit and q-bio.GN cross-list; the arXiv record gives NeurIPS 2026 as publication venue; evaluated across four paired single-cell datasets.

sections.title: Geometric Relevance Is Not Sufficient: Evaluating Focused Post-Training Supervision in Diffusion Docking
sections.abstract: A fixed-budget DiffDock study compares broad continuation with focused torsional supervision and finds no consistent advantage for focused strategies on the reported docking endpoints.
sections.claimed_contribution: In an evaluation of 99 complexes with three training seeds, broad continuation had the highest mean trained-policy Top-1 success below 5 Å; focused or mixed supervision did not consistently improve on broad continuation within the tested budget.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a computational result for one architecture, one test set, a five-epoch budget, and one sampling seed. Confidence selection and physical/external confirmation remain unresolved.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct molecular-docking relevance; accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 AI4DD Workshop; evaluates score fidelity, pose recovery, best-of-10 sampling, and Top-1 selection separately.
sections.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 AI4DD Workshop.

sections.title: How Deep is the Signal? Time-Context up to 30 Years for Colorectal Cancer Prediction in a Primary-Care EHR Model
sections.abstract: This study tests how far back a primary-care EHR model needs to look to predict incident colorectal cancer using nested calendar-time lookback windows.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report AUROC rising from 0.551 with a two-year lookback to 0.590 at 18 years before plateauing; XGBoost reached a similar peak of 0.589. They propose calendar-time context as a distinct EHR model-design variable.
sections.unique_caveat: This retrospective prediction study uses one North West London health system and reports modest discrimination without prospective or clinical-utility evaluation; it is not evidence of a validated screening test.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted at Machine Learning for Health 2026 (Findings Track); frozen cohort of 1,008 cases and 9,582 matched controls, pretrained on 3.6 million primary-care patients.
sections.journal_ref: Machine Learning for Health (ML4H) 2026, Findings Track

sections.title: Resampling-based batch reweighting for ComBat harmonization of MRI radiomic features in a multi-scanner glioma cohort
sections.abstract: A revised study tests whether reweighting underrepresented scanner batches before ComBat estimation reduces residual scanner effects in glioma MRI radiomic features.
sections.claimed_contribution: In a retrospective, single-centre Erasmus Glioma Database cohort of 733 patients across nine scanner configurations, the authors report 13/428 features with significant residual scanner association after standard ComBat versus 8/428 with batch-augmented ComBat.
sections.unique_caveat: This remains a single-centre radiomics harmonization analysis; the reported reduction does not establish external generalization or improved patient outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Substantive v2 revision in the latest announcement batch and direct medical-imaging relevance; the arXiv record says the article was submitted to the Journal of Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
sections.comment: Original article. Submitted to Journal of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (JMRI).

sections.title: Accelerating reaction network identification via frequency-domain analysis
sections.abstract: The authors report that Fourier-domain measurements can make likelihoods approximately Gaussian in some intracellular reaction systems, enabling faster Bayesian network inference in an illustrative transcription example.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors identify a condition under which a Fourier transform approximately Gaussianizes the measurement likelihood and use it to construct an accelerated Bayesian inference algorithm.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports one illustrative example, not broad experimental validation; the approximation is stated to apply only to certain systems.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Primary category q-bio.MN and direct relevance to intracellular reaction-network inference; the abstract illustrates the approach with gene transcription.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.summary: The selected papers repeatedly emphasize evaluation beyond single proxy metrics: BILBY contrasts static recovery with MD-supported dynamics, while the docking paper separates score fidelity, pose recovery, and confidence selection. MUSS models relationships between sequence and cell-level regulation; PharmAgents2 organizes decisions across discovery workflows and reports human-run assay follow-up. The colorectal EHR and glioma MRI papers evaluate retrospective models on clinical data but do not establish prospective clinical utility. These observations describe this small selected batch, not a field-wide shift.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.summary: PharmAgents2 motivates independent replication and orthogonal tests of target engagement and LpxH mechanism; BILBY motivates longer or replicated dynamics simulations plus experimental stability/activity assays. MUSS needs independent tissue, assay, and perturbation tests. The EHR and MRI studies need external temporal/geographic cohort or scanner-site validation before utility claims. The reaction-network approximation should be tested against particle-filtering and independent measurements across additional topologies, noise levels, and cell systems.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.summary: The batch’s clearest contribution is methodological: biological AI systems need evaluation against dynamic, held-out, or externally measured outcomes, not only convenient proxy metrics. PharmAgents2 reports human-executed assays, which are early discovery findings rather than clinical validation; the other selected studies remain computational or retrospective and are bounded by their validation designs.
